newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says speed of NZ dollar rise is of concern.
newsitem.headline: Peters says speed of NZ dollar rise is of concern.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday that the speed of the New Zealand dollar's rise was of more concern than the rise itself.

Peters also said that extra government spending would be "not a dollar" more or less than the NZ$1.2 billion agreed between his New Zealand First party and the conservative National Party in last month's coalition accord.
"It will not cost more than $1.2 billion," he said of the extra spending package agreed by the coalition government for 1997/98.
"We (the New Zealand First Party) asked for expenditure of $1.2 billion on critical areas of what you might call investment in social neglect," Peters told reporters.
"That is what we intend to have spent, not a dollar more, not a dollar less," he said.
"It's the speed of its recent rise that is probably of more concern as much as the rise itself," Peters said of the New Zealand dollar.
Peters said he had campaigned in last year's election on efficient government and said there was still a lot of fat in government.
"That's what I'm interested in looking at now. Is the purpose still as efficacious as it once was. Those are the sort of things we want to look at, and government charges as well," he said.
Asked about his reluctance to comment on the dollar after vigorously campaining against a high dollar, Peters said he did not want to be rushed into action.
He said he wanted to appoint an independent economic advisor in the next few days.
Cabinet had its first meeting of the year on Tuesday but Peters declined to comment on what was discussed.
